key_insight: PolicyIK treats inverse kinematics as a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning problem, aiming to translate desired robot-hand positions and orientations into precise joint motion.
problem_solved: Precise robot-arm control is difficult because multiple joint configurations can reach the same target, singularities complicate movement, controllers require hand-tuning, and physical training data are costly.
method: Represent the desired end-effector position and orientation as the policy's goal.
Use reinforcement learning to learn joint updates for inverse kinematics.
Target high-precision motion; training details and measured performance are not available in the provided, truncated abstract.
impact: A learned IK policy could support more precise execution of vision-language-action commands and help transfer them between robot arms. The provided excerpt does not establish accuracy gains or cross-robot transfer results.
visual_elements: Pipeline: target pose → goal-conditioned PolicyIK → joint motion → robot-hand pose.
Robot-arm overlay showing the current pose, target pose, and position/orientation error.
Side-by-side arm configurations illustrating multiple ways to reach one target.

paper_title: PolicyIK: High-Precision Inverse Kinematics for Robot Arms with Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Yuhan Liu, Xinqi Liu, Zixuan Dong, Keith W. Ross, Shenji Wan
